title: A Restaurant Critic (Ours) On the Year That Changed Him Forever

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin，我是 Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带上 300 件你最珍视的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: I'm an audio professional.
sentences.zh: 我是一名音频专业人士。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Good to see you in ages.
sentences.zh: 好久不见了。

sentences.en: Nice to see you, Pete.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你，Pete。

sentences.en: How have you been?
sentences.zh: 你最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Well, you know, the last four years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，过去这四年。

sentences.en: You know.
sentences.zh: 你懂的。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, that's right now.
sentences.zh: 是啊，嗯，现在就是这样。

sentences.en: Okay, Pete, so we're going to put this on.
sentences.zh: 好了，Pete，我们要把这个戴上。

sentences.en: What's...
sentences.zh: 这是……

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 我看看。

sentences.en: Can we find like a...
sentences.zh: 我们能找到一个……

sentences.en: Maybe like a lapel here?
sentences.zh: 也许是领口这里？

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 这样就行。

sentences.en: So, Pete, I just want to explain to people what's happening here.
sentences.zh: Pete，我想向大家解释一下现在的情况。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, it is around 6.45 on a Friday night.
sentences.zh: 现在是周五晚上 6 点 45 分左右。

sentences.en: Pete Wells just arrived.
sentences.zh: Pete Wells 刚到。

sentences.en: The famed New York Times restaurant critic.
sentences.zh: 那位著名的《纽约时报》餐厅评论家。

sentences.en: He's now opening his shirt in the middle of a public park in Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 他现在正站在唐人街的一个公园中央解开衬衫扣子。

sentences.en: My brother took a photo.
sentences.zh: 我兄弟拍了张照片。

sentences.en: So that a microphone can be affixed to his shirt.
sentences.zh: 为了把麦克风别在他的衬衫上。

sentences.en: So that we might surreptitiously dine with you and experience firsthand what it's like to review a restaurant for the August New York Times.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就能悄悄地和你一起用餐，亲身体验为《纽约时报》八月刊撰写餐厅评论是什么感觉。

sentences.en: And it's quite a sight to behold.
sentences.zh: 这场景真是相当壮观。

sentences.en: This open-shirted mic application.
sentences.zh: 这种在敞开的衬衫上别麦克风的场面。

sentences.en: I don't know how surreptitious we really are, but we'll...
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们到底有多“悄悄”，但我们会……

sentences.en: I think...
sentences.zh: 我想……

sentences.en: So, I really think this is going to work because these laugh mics are really subtle, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，我真的觉得这招行得通，因为这些领夹麦克风非常隐蔽，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I don't think we're going to...
sentences.zh: 我不觉得我们会……

sentences.en: We're going to get discovered.
sentences.zh: 我们会露馅的。

sentences.en: Very John LeCourre.
sentences.zh: 很有约翰·勒卡雷（John Le Carré）间谍小说的感觉。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的 Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》节目。

sentences.en: Throughout his time as the restaurant critic for The Times, Pete Wells has become the single
sentences.zh: 在担任《纽约时报》餐厅评论家的这段时间里，Pete Wells 已经成为了美食界

sentences.en: most revered and feared voice in the world of fine dining, crowning its newest stars and dethroning those whose time has passed.
sentences.zh: 最受推崇也最令人畏惧的声音，他为新星加冕，也将那些过气的餐厅拉下神坛。

sentences.en: Then, everything changed.
sentences.zh: 然后，一切都变了。

sentences.en: Most of all, Wells himself.
sentences.zh: 尤其是 Wells 本人。

sentences.en: Today, a conversation over dinner with Pete Wells.
sentences.zh: 今天，与 Pete Wells 共进晚餐并进行一场对话。

sentences.en: It's Friday, December 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是 12 月 23 日，星期五。

sentences.en: Pete, I want to start by asking you about your relationship to food.
sentences.zh: Pete，我想先问问你与食物之间的关系。

sentences.en: I mean, what is it?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那是什么样的关系？

sentences.en: Outside of your job, what is your earliest relationship to dining?
sentences.zh: 除了工作之外，你最早与餐饮的接触是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I never went to nice restaurants as a kid.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我小时候从不去高档餐厅。

sentences.en: I mean, the fanciest restaurant I remember going to as a kid was in Providence.
sentences.zh: 我记得小时候去过最高档的餐厅是在普罗维登斯。

sentences.en: It was this place called the Rusty Scupper.
sentences.zh: 那家店叫“Rusty Scupper”。

sentences.en: And the menu was like printed on an oar.
sentences.zh: 菜单是印在一支船桨上的。

sentences.en: I'm laughing because I know that place and it is very basic.
sentences.zh: 我笑是因为我知道那家店，它真的很普通。

sentences.en: But, you know, baked stuffed shrimp to me at 12 was like mind-blowing.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，12 岁时吃到烤酿虾对我来说简直是惊为天人。

sentences.en: How they got the menu on the side of the oar, I will never figure out, you know.
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么把菜单印在船桨侧面的，我永远也想不通。

sentences.en: There might have been tablecloths.
sentences.zh: 桌上可能铺了桌布。

sentences.en: There probably was like a bread basket that came around.
sentences.zh: 可能还会送上一篮面包。

sentences.en: There's definitely lobster bibs.
sentences.zh: 肯定有龙虾围兜。

sentences.en: And there were definitely lobster bibs.
sentences.zh: 而且绝对有龙虾围兜。

sentences.en: So, you know, that was kind of my world growing up.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，那就是我成长过程中的世界。

sentences.en: And it didn't get fancier when I was like a young writer starting out in New York City.
sentences.zh: 当我年轻时在纽约市刚开始写作时，生活也没有变得更奢华。

sentences.en: I mean, I ate burritos three times a week.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我每周吃三次墨西哥卷饼。

sentences.en: You know, I ate tons of pierogies in the East Village.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我在东村吃过无数的波兰饺子。

sentences.en: And the very first restaurant assignment I ever got was to write about cheap restaurants in the East Village.
sentences.zh: 我接到的第一个餐厅任务就是写关于东村廉价餐厅的文章。

sentences.en: Right, this was your world.
sentences.zh: 没错，这就是你的世界。

sentences.en: Yes, right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: So this is back in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 那是 90 年代的事了。

sentences.en: So this was kind of how it started.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是一切开始的方式。

sentences.en: But I didn't think of myself as a restaurant person at all.
sentences.zh: 但我从没想过自己会成为一个“餐厅达人”。

sentences.en: And I mostly cooked at home.
sentences.zh: 我大部分时间都在家里做饭。

sentences.en: And that was my whole frame of reference.
sentences.zh: 这就是我全部的参考框架。

sentences.en: Home cooking and how much cheaper it was to, you know, have your friends over to a meal that you cooked yourself than to go out to some place that somebody else picked.
sentences.zh: 家常菜，而且邀请朋友来吃你自己做的饭，比去别人选的地方吃饭要便宜得多。

sentences.en: I was always shocked by the bill, you know.
sentences.zh: 我总是被账单吓到，你知道的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Well, given, Pete, your love for the pierogies and the burritos of the world and your passion as a home cook,
sentences.zh: 好吧，Pete，考虑到你对波兰饺子和墨西哥卷饼的热爱，以及你作为家庭厨师的热情，

sentences.en: I'm curious how you saw your mission once you were crowned New York Times restaurant critic
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，当你被加冕为《纽约时报》餐厅评论家，

sentences.en: and you became this exceptionally influential writer whose job is very much focused on high-end dining in New York.
sentences.zh: 成为一位极具影响力、工作重心高度集中在纽约高端餐饮界的作家后，你是如何看待自己的使命的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, no one hands you a list of the rules of restaurant criticism.
sentences.zh: 是的，没人会给你一份餐厅评论的规则清单。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I thought the job was to help readers figure out what was worth the money.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这份工作的意义在于帮助读者弄清楚什么东西物有所值。

sentences.en: So in other words, like, there are a lot of expensive restaurants you can run through buckets and buckets and buckets of money
sentences.zh: 换句话说，有很多昂贵的餐厅，你可以花掉大把大把的钱，

sentences.en: just keeping up with all the expensive restaurants that open in New York.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了跟上纽约新开的那些昂贵餐厅的步伐。

sentences.en: And I was very aware that, like, the normal person cannot run to every new restaurant that opens.
sentences.zh: 我非常清楚，普通人不可能跑遍每一家新开的餐厅。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: So I thought an important part of the job was sorting through all this really expensive stuff and telling people, okay, this is worth your money.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这份工作的一个重要部分，就是从这些昂贵的东西中筛选出来，告诉人们：好吧，这个值得你花钱。

sentences.en: This is a splurge.
sentences.zh: 这个值得挥霍一下。

sentences.en: This I wouldn't bother with.
sentences.zh: 这个我就不推荐了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Because, you know, I had that experience that we've all had of walking into something that you think is going to be great
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，我们都有过那种经历：走进一家你以为会很棒的餐厅，

sentences.en: and then, you know, just really feeling like a sucker when you're signing the check, you know?
sentences.zh: 结果在签账单时真的觉得自己像个冤大头，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Like, wow, I really got taken.
sentences.zh: 就像是，哇，我真的被坑了。

sentences.en: Or maybe there's something wrong with me.
sentences.zh: 或者也许是我自己有问题。

sentences.en: Maybe I didn't appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 也许我没能欣赏它。

sentences.en: Maybe I ordered the wrong things, you know?
sentences.zh: 也许是我点错菜了，你知道吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But whatever it is, it's an unpleasant experience, right?
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，这都是一种不愉快的体验，对吧？

sentences.en: Awful feeling.
sentences.zh: 糟糕的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the way, of course, that you tell people that they're not going to get fleeced is through a system of assigning stars to restaurants.
sentences.zh: 当然，你告诉人们他们不会被宰的方法，是通过一套给餐厅评星的系统。

sentences.en: So can you just walk us through that?
sentences.zh: 你能带我们了解一下吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, the stars are supposed to be kind of summing up of the review.
sentences.zh: 嗯，星级应该是对评论的一种总结。

sentences.en: I think for some readers, they're the entire review.
sentences.zh: 我想对一些读者来说，这就是全部的评论了。

sentences.en: They just look at the star and they say, oh, well, then we're going to go there.
sentences.zh: 他们只看星星，然后说，哦，那我们就去那儿吧。

sentences.en: Or we'll put that on the liSt.
sentences.zh: 或者我们会把它加进清单里。

sentences.en: But what they're supposed to signify, and we used to run a little explainer every week that decoded them that said stars reflect the reviewer's reaction to service, atmosphere,
sentences.zh: 但它们本应代表的含义——我们过去每周都会刊登一个小说明来解读它们——是星级反映了评论家对服务、氛围、

sentences.en: and food with price taken into account.
sentences.zh: 以及食物的反应，同时考虑了价格因素。

sentences.en: So one star is good.
sentences.zh: 所以一颗星代表好。

sentences.en: Two is very good.
sentences.zh: 两颗星代表非常好。

sentences.en: Three, I believe, is excellent.
sentences.zh: 三颗星，我想是极好。

sentences.en: And four is extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 四颗星则是非凡。

sentences.en: Whatever that means to you, or to, I guess, whatever it means to me is the, you know, the relevant concept.
sentences.zh: 无论这对你意味着什么，或者我想，无论这对我意味着什么，才是相关的概念。

sentences.en: And well, what does extraordinary mean, Pete, to you?
sentences.zh: 那么，Pete，对你来说“非凡”意味着什么？

sentences.en: You start with the idea that there can only be a small handful of extraordinary restaurants in the city at any one time.
sentences.zh: 你首先要有一个概念，即在任何特定时间，城里只能有少数几家非凡的餐厅。

sentences.en: I think it's only meaningful if extraordinary is very, very hard to get.
sentences.zh: 我认为只有当“非凡”非常、非常难达到时，它才有意义。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: In my mind, it was a striving for perfection or as close to it as, you know, one could come.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，那是一种对完美的追求，或者说是尽可能接近完美。

sentences.en: And restaurants are unbelievably complex organisms with all these moving parts, and they're based on humans who screw up all the time.
sentences.zh: 餐厅是极其复杂的有机体，有这么多运转的部件，而且它们的基础是随时会犯错的人类。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you have to understand that it's not going to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须明白，它不可能完美无缺。

sentences.en: But when it seems like it maybe almost is, you realize how much went into creating that.
sentences.zh: 但当它看起来几乎完美时，你会意识到为了创造这一切付出了多少努力。

sentences.en: To me, that's really impressive.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这真的很令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Okay, well, with that in mind, I want to talk through a couple of your reviews.
sentences.zh: 好的，考虑到这一点，我想讨论一下你的几篇评论。

sentences.en: And I want to start, since we're on the subject of extraordinary restaurants, with a restaurant that you designated thusly,
sentences.zh: 既然我们谈到了非凡餐厅的话题，我想从你指定的一家餐厅开始，

sentences.en: which is Le Bernardin, the French restaurant in Midtown, that you reviewed back in 2012.
sentences.zh: 那就是 Le Bernardin，位于中城的法式餐厅，你曾在 2012 年评论过它。

sentences.en: So could I ask you to read from your review of that restaurant?
sentences.zh: 我能请你读一下你对那家餐厅的评论吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Some of the thrills are the hushed kind, like the way black garlic, pomegranate, and lime support the crisp skin and white flesh of sautéed black bass.
sentences.zh: 有些惊喜是静谧的，比如黑蒜、石榴和青柠如何衬托出香煎黑鲈鱼酥脆的鱼皮和洁白的鱼肉。

sentences.en: Others are scene-stealers, as when a white slab of steamed halibut is slowly surrounded by a crimson pool of beet sauce,
sentences.zh: 另一些则是抢镜的，比如当一块清蒸大比目鱼被一圈深红色的甜菜酱慢慢包围时，

sentences.en: that, with creme fraiche stirred in, will turn the delirious pink of summer borscht.
sentences.zh: 加入法式酸奶油搅拌后，它会变成夏季罗宋汤那种令人迷醉的粉红色。

sentences.en: That last dish sounds like a restaurant striving for perfection.
sentences.zh: 最后那道菜听起来就像是一家追求完美的餐厅。

sentences.en: It's great.
sentences.zh: 它很棒。

sentences.en: I mean, it's still great.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它依然很棒。

sentences.en: It's still great.
sentences.zh: 它依然很棒。

sentences.en: It is a version of what extraordinary can be.
sentences.zh: 这就是“非凡”可能呈现的一种版本。

sentences.en: We should say, and I've been searching around as we've been talking, that this is no inexpensive meal.
sentences.zh: 我们应该说明一下——我在谈话时查了一下——这可不是一顿便宜的饭。

sentences.en: Le Bernardin is a nearly $200 four-course dinner and a $120 three-course lunch.
sentences.zh: Le Bernardin 的四道菜晚餐近 200 美元，三道菜午餐 120 美元。

sentences.en: So, real money.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是真金白银。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You're definitely, you're paying for it.
sentences.zh: 你确实是在为它买单。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But you're saying with four stars, you're paying for it, and it's actually worth it.
sentences.zh: 但你的意思是，给出四星评价，说明你付了钱，而且它确实物有所值。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: But of course, the reviews of yours that I've especially loved, and that I know many others have loved as well, are when you have not always found the trade to be fair.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我特别喜欢的你的评论，而且我知道许多其他人也喜欢的，是你发现交易并不公平的时候。

sentences.en: And that's because sometimes you've eviscerated restaurants for not fulfilling the pledge to be worth their price.
sentences.zh: 那是因为有时你曾严厉抨击过那些未能兑现其价格承诺的餐厅。

sentences.en: And I think the one that is best known is your review of Per Se, which is Thomas Keller's Temple to Haute Cuisine atop the Time Warner Center in Columbus Circle in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 我想最广为人知的一篇应该是你对Per Se的评论，那是托马斯·凯勒（Thomas Keller）在曼哈顿哥伦布圆环时代华纳中心顶层打造的高级烹饪殿堂。

sentences.en: I wonder if you can read a few lines from that review.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能不能读一下那篇评论里的几行文字。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Dinner or lunch at this grand, hermetic, self-regarding, ungenerous restaurant brings a protracted march of many dishes.
sentences.zh: 在这家宏大、封闭、自视甚高且吝啬的餐厅里，晚餐或午餐意味着一道接一道菜肴的漫长行军。

sentences.en: And then I go into some examples.
sentences.zh: 然后我列举了一些例子。

sentences.en: I don't know what could have saved limp, dispiriting yam dumplings, but it definitely wasn't a lukewarm Matsutake mushroom bouillon as murky and appealing as bong water.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有什么能拯救那些软塌塌、令人沮丧的山药饺子，但绝对不是那碗温吞的松茸清汤，它浑浊不堪，看起来就像洗烟斗的水一样诱人。

sentences.en: When my server asked, would you like the foie gras, $40 more, or the salad, the question had an air of menace.
sentences.zh: 当服务员问我是否要加40美元来份鹅肝，或者选沙拉时，那个问题透着一股威胁的气息。

sentences.en: When the salad turned out to be a pale, uncrisp, fried eggplant raviolo next to droopy strips of red pepper and carrot, it felt like extortion.
sentences.zh: 当沙拉端上来，竟是一块苍白、不脆的炸茄子饺，旁边配着蔫掉的红椒和胡萝卜条时，感觉就像被勒索了一样。

sentences.en: And I go through a few more things like that, and then I conclude,
sentences.zh: 我接着又写了一些类似的事情，然后总结道：

sentences.en: Per Se is among the worst food deals in New York.
sentences.zh: Per Se是纽约最不划算的餐饮消费之一。

sentences.en: It's just a terrible value for the money you're spending.
sentences.zh: 对于你花的钱来说，这简直太不值了。

sentences.en: Well, can you just explain the value?
sentences.zh: 那么，你能解释一下这个价值吗？

sentences.en: Because I don't think everybody necessarily knows the price.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得大家未必都知道价格。

sentences.en: Well, so at the time, there was a tasting menu that was, at dinner, $325,
sentences.zh: 当时，晚餐的品鉴菜单是325美元，

sentences.en: and you got nine courses.
sentences.zh: 你可以吃到九道菜。

sentences.en: But then I just mentioned, would you like the foie gras for $40 more?
sentences.zh: 但就像我刚才提到的，他们会问你要不要加40美元来份鹅肝？

sentences.en: There were a lot of upsells like that.
sentences.zh: 像这样的加价推销有很多。

sentences.en: And if you got all of them, you'd find yourself spending quite a bit more money than $325.
sentences.zh: 如果你全都要了，你会发现自己花的钱远不止325美元。

sentences.en: I ended up, in one of those meals, spending $3,000 or close to it for four people.
sentences.zh: 有一次用餐，我最终花了3000美元，或者接近这个数，那是四个人的费用。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I know it still feels, I mean, I feel something in my stomach right now when I'm saying it, which is like, oh my goodness, wow.
sentences.zh: 我知道这听起来还是很……我是说，我现在说出来的时候胃里都有种感觉，就像是，天哪，哇。

sentences.en: How can that be?
sentences.zh: 怎么会这样呢？

sentences.en: Right, for bong water.
sentences.zh: 没错，为了那碗洗烟斗水。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, can you remind us how many stars you gave, Per Se?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你能提醒我们你给了Per Se几颗星吗？

sentences.en: Yes, this one was two because it was such a move down from the four that it had previously carried.
sentences.zh: 是的，这次是两颗星，因为它比之前一直保持的四颗星水准下降了太多。

sentences.en: I settled on two because I thought, boy, I mean, can you take all four stars away at the same time?
sentences.zh: 我最终决定给两颗星，因为我想，天哪，难道能一下子把四颗星全拿走吗？

sentences.en: Is that even how it works?
sentences.zh: 这是行得通的吗？

sentences.en: I remember feeling kind of sick because I was going to have to drop this bomb.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时感觉有点恶心，因为我不得不投下这枚重磅炸弹。

sentences.en: And it did kind of go off like a bomb.
sentences.zh: 它确实像炸弹一样引爆了。

sentences.en: I recall this review really well, Pete.
sentences.zh: 皮特，我对那篇评论记忆犹新。

sentences.en: And in my memory, it wasn't that you gave it two stars.
sentences.zh: 在我的记忆里，重点不在于你给了它两颗星。

sentences.en: It was that you took away two stars.
sentences.zh: 而在于你拿走了两颗星。

sentences.en: Well, that's how it's perceived for sure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大家确实是这么理解的。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: One of New York City's best-rated restaurants just got eviscerated by New York Times restaurant critic Pete Wells.
sentences.zh: 纽约市评价最高的餐厅之一，刚刚被《纽约时报》餐厅评论家皮特·威尔斯（Pete Wells）狠狠地抨击了一番。

sentences.en: Pete Wells knocked half of Per Se's stars off of its marquee.
sentences.zh: 皮特·威尔斯抹掉了Per Se招牌上的一半星级。

sentences.en: It was last reviewed in 2011 by the Times then-critic Sam Sifton.
sentences.zh: 它上一次被《时报》评论是在2011年，由当时的时报评论家萨姆·西夫顿（Sam Sifton）执笔。

sentences.en: But in his latest review, out today, Wells downgraded the eatery to two stars.
sentences.zh: 但在今天发布的最新评论中，威尔斯将这家餐厅降级为两颗星。

sentences.en: Two, and the restaurant was dull at best, disappointing and flat-footed among the worst food deals in New York.
sentences.zh: 两颗星，而且这家餐厅充其量只是乏味，在纽约最糟糕的餐饮消费中，它令人失望且反应迟钝。

sentences.en: Look, you're the food sheriff, you're on the beat, you're warning people, that's a crime scene down there, don't go.
sentences.zh: 听着，你是美食警长，你在巡逻，你在警告人们，那下面是犯罪现场，别去。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The soup probably wasn't that bad.
sentences.zh: 那汤可能没那么糟糕。

sentences.en: But I'm just wondering, like, how would he know what that kind of water tastes like?
sentences.zh: 但我只是在想，他怎么会知道那种水是什么味道的？

sentences.en: Is that a weird question to ask?
sentences.zh: 这个问题很奇怪吗？

sentences.en: But if somebody who maybe doesn't have $300 to waste gets the message and goes and spends it somewhere else,
sentences.zh: 但如果有人可能没有300美元可以浪费，却收到了这个信息，转而去别处消费，

sentences.en: you know, it's worth it, I guess.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想这还是值得的。

sentences.en: Boy, people can be pretty mean, can't they?
sentences.zh: 天哪，人们有时候真的很刻薄，不是吗？

sentences.en: But Pete, as much as you might have been administering a certain kind of food justice here,
sentences.zh: 但皮特，尽管你可能是在这里行使某种美食正义，

sentences.en: these two reviews we're talking about, Le Bernardin, per se, in a lot of ways, they uphold a certain system and vision of dining that is very high-end, right?
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的这两篇评论，关于Le Bernardin和Per Se，在很多方面，它们都在维护一种非常高端的餐饮体系和愿景，对吧？

sentences.en: And I've read almost all your reviews.
sentences.zh: 我读过你几乎所有的评论。

sentences.en: You know, by and large, you spend a lot of time at expensive restaurants that are striving for greatness.
sentences.zh: 你知道，总的来说，你花了很多时间在那些追求卓越的昂贵餐厅里。

sentences.en: And as much as you might be taking away two stars from a restaurant that's a ripoff, in some ways, the very act of reviewing it says to the world that this is where it's at,
sentences.zh: 尽管你可能从一家坑人的餐厅拿走了两颗星，但在某种程度上，评论它这一行为本身就是在向世界宣告，这就是顶尖所在，

sentences.en: and this is where your food focus should be.
sentences.zh: 这就是你们应该关注的美食焦点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't think there's a way out of it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得没法摆脱这一点。

sentences.en: I would try to mix it up.
sentences.zh: 我会试着换换口味。

sentences.en: And if I'd gone to too many places where I was sitting on a cushy padding where my butt was kind of floating three inches off the chair,
sentences.zh: 如果我去了太多地方，坐在那种软垫上，屁股离椅子有三英寸高，

sentences.en: if I did that too many nights in a row and they were always refilling my water glass, I would think, oh, you've got to get real for a minute here and go somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 如果我连续好几个晚上都这样，而且他们总是给我续水，我会想，哦，你得清醒一下，去别的地方看看。

sentences.en: Right, right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: But you'd always end up with your butt hanging in the air, right?
sentences.zh: 但你最终还是会屁股悬空，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's the, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是，是的。

sentences.en: So, I'll wake up on a Monday morning and before the end of the week, I will have, you know, signed off on some check that's shocking,
sentences.zh: 所以，我会在周一早上醒来，在周末结束之前，我已经签下了一张令人震惊的支票，

sentences.en: six or seven or eight hundred or nine hundred dollars.
sentences.zh: 六百、七百、八百或九百美元。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a very large sum, and I'm going to send it off to the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 这是一笔非常大的金额，我会把它寄给《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: And that's just how it's going to be.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样。

sentences.en: And then it stopped being that way.
sentences.zh: 然后情况就不一样了。

sentences.en: I mean, once the pandemic came, you couldn't even spend that kind of money on a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 我是说，一旦疫情来袭，你甚至没法在餐厅花那种钱了。

sentences.en: First of all, there were no restaurants.
sentences.zh: 首先，根本没有餐厅营业。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, and that lasted for months and months and months.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这种情况持续了好几个月。

sentences.en: And then when restaurants opened again with outdoor dining only, ah, I was so relieved I get to go eat again.
sentences.zh: 然后当餐厅重新开放，只提供户外用餐时，啊，我太欣慰了，我又能去吃饭了。

sentences.en: But Per Se wasn't doing outdoor dining.
sentences.zh: 但Per Se没有做户外用餐。

sentences.en: Leperto Dan wasn't doing outdoor dining.
sentences.zh: Le Bernardin也没有做户外用餐。

sentences.en: Any of the places that had four stars or aspired to four stars, they didn't have a little sidewalk patio.
sentences.zh: 任何拥有四颗星或渴望四颗星的地方，都没有小人行道露台。

sentences.en: They didn't have a plywood hut.
sentences.zh: 他们没有胶合板搭的小棚子。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So very quickly, the upper crust that is very central to your job has literally gone away.
sentences.zh: 所以很快，你工作中非常核心的那部分上流社会实际上已经消失了。

sentences.en: It's gone.
sentences.zh: 它消失了。

sentences.en: It's not there.
sentences.zh: 它不在了。

sentences.en: And the first day that outdoor dining came back, I went out for the first meal, which was lunch, and rode my bike around until I could find a place.
sentences.zh: 户外用餐恢复的第一天，我出去吃了第一顿饭，那是午餐，我骑着自行车到处转，直到找到一家店。

sentences.en: And then that was kind of life for a while, was me on my bike, sitting out on the sidewalk, and there was just no fanciness left at all.
sentences.zh: 那段时间的生活就是这样，我骑着车，坐在人行道上，完全没有了任何奢华感。

sentences.en: Trucks and carts and places that were you just, you sat on the sidewalk at this table that was about to fall over.
sentences.zh: 卡车、餐车，还有那些你坐在人行道上，桌子快要倒了的地方。

sentences.en: Right, and there's not a piece of halibut with beet sauce in sight.
sentences.zh: 没错，而且根本看不到什么配甜菜酱的大比目鱼。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有。

sentences.en: Nobody who was surviving the pandemic was trying to create the perfect meal.
sentences.zh: 没有谁在疫情中幸存下来的人还在试图创造完美的餐点。

sentences.en: They were just trying to create a meal.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在试图创造一顿饭。

sentences.en: A meal, right.
sentences.zh: 一顿饭，对吧。

sentences.en: A meal.
sentences.zh: 一顿饭。

sentences.en: So I started going to them, and they were just completely different from my usual diet.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始去这些地方，它们和我平时的饮食完全不同。

sentences.en: You know, this was like a bar in Midtown by the Empire State Building.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就像是帝国大厦附近中城的一家酒吧。

sentences.en: There was a Chapley kebab truck way, way out in Queens, almost not even a chef who had been doing this pop-up out of somebody else's restaurant.
sentences.zh: 皇后区很远的地方有一辆Chapley烤肉车，甚至几乎不是一个厨师，只是在别人的餐厅里做快闪店。

sentences.en: This was like a wild, creative leap just based.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一次疯狂的、创造性的飞跃。

sentences.en: You know, the first time I went, I ordered and sat on the hood of my car, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我第一次去的时候，点完餐就坐在我的车盖上吃，你知道的。

sentences.en: So I wanted to write about them, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我很想写写他们，对吧？

sentences.en: But it didn't make sense to review them the way I used to review.
sentences.zh: 但用我过去那种方式去评论他们并不合理。

sentences.en: And it definitely didn't make sense to you of stars.
sentences.zh: 而且用星级来评价他们绝对不合理。

sentences.en: That was just, like, how could you compare a restaurant that was doing outdoor dining only during the pandemic with maybe one cook and one waiter,
sentences.zh: 那简直是，你怎么能把疫情期间只提供户外用餐、可能只有一个厨师和一个服务员的餐厅，

sentences.en: or sometimes the cook is the waiter.
sentences.zh: 或者有时厨师就是服务员的餐厅，拿来比较呢？

sentences.en: How could you compare that to, like, what restaurants used to do and what my whole notion of, like, what one, two, three, four stars meant didn't make any sense to go in
sentences.zh: 你怎么能把它和餐厅过去的做法相比？我关于一、二、三、四颗星意味着什么的整个概念，在去说：

sentences.en: and say, you know, they have the ugliest assortment of chairs and tables I've ever seen.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们有我见过最丑的桌椅组合，这根本没有任何意义。

sentences.en: You just, people were working under the most extenuating circumstances you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 你只是，人们是在你能想象到的最极端的情况下工作。

sentences.en: There was, you know, it would have just seemed...
sentences.zh: 这，你知道，这看起来会……

sentences.en: Gratuitous.
sentences.zh: 多余。

sentences.en: Stupid.
sentences.zh: 愚蠢。

sentences.en: That's just gratuitous, but just, like, don't you see what's going on here, my man?
sentences.zh: 那只是多余，但就像是，你没看到这里发生了什么吗，伙计？

sentences.en: Don't you see that these people are, like, one step away from bankruptcy?
sentences.zh: 你没看到这些人离破产只有一步之遥吗？

sentences.en: Like, can't you feel that, like, if they could do a better job, they would?
sentences.zh: 就像，你感觉不到如果他们能做得更好，他们会去做吗？

sentences.en: But this is what they can do right now?
sentences.zh: 但这就是他们现在能做到的全部了？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, what did you see your role in this moment?
sentences.zh: 那么，你如何看待你在这一时刻的角色？

sentences.en: Because from everything you're saying, you're suddenly a food critic who is rooting for all these restaurants who are so desperate just to survive.
sentences.zh: 因为从你所说的一切来看，你突然变成了一个支持所有这些拼命求生存的餐厅的美食评论家。

sentences.en: Well, the part of the job that used to be about saying, this is good, this is acceptable, this is not very good, that all seemed irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 嗯，工作中曾经关于说“这很好，这可以接受，这不太好”的部分，似乎都变得无关紧要了。

sentences.en: And what was more interesting was saying, this is interesting over here, this is interesting over there, there's something happening here you might want to know about.
sentences.zh: 更有趣的是说“这边很有趣，那边很有趣，这里有些事情你可能想了解一下”。

sentences.en: And that started to seem like something I could really run with.
sentences.zh: 这开始看起来像是我真正可以投入的事情。

sentences.en: So rather than just sorting extraordinary, excellent, very good, good, fair, poor, satisfactory,
sentences.zh: 所以与其只是进行非凡、优秀、很好、好、一般、差、令人满意的分类，

sentences.en: the point would be connecting.
sentences.zh: 重点在于连接。

sentences.en: Connecting readers to things that they could get excited about that they might not have known about.
sentences.zh: 将读者与他们可能感兴趣但之前不知道的事物连接起来。

sentences.en: And of course, this is not a new thing in food writing.
sentences.zh: 当然，这在美食写作中并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: It's not a new thing in New York City.
sentences.zh: 在纽约市也不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: It was just, it hadn't really been a major part of my job before.
sentences.zh: 只是，它之前并没有真正成为我工作的主要部分。

sentences.en: So it just started to seem like,
sentences.zh: 所以它开始看起来像是，

sentences.en: well, you know, why have I been so narrow-minded?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我为什么一直这么狭隘？

sentences.en: Why am I trying to impose my ideas of what a restaurant should be on what's really out there?
sentences.zh: 为什么我要把关于餐厅应该是什么样的想法强加给现实中存在的东西？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金（Andrew Ross-Sorkin）。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯DealBook报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的领导者，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯（Vance）、埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德（Christine Lagarde）、

sentences.en: Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: Zylran Mondani以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com为所有人免费直播部分采访。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过的。

sentences.en: So Pete, how does the world, and how do your bosses at the Times, respond to this new version of yourself as a critic, one who doesn't use the stars,
sentences.zh: 那么皮特，世界以及《时报》的老板们，是如何回应你作为评论家的新形象的？一个不用星级，

sentences.en: and one who sees the role as this connector rather than a sorter?
sentences.zh: 一个将角色视为连接者而非分类者的评论家？

sentences.en: Well, there were some people who didn't get it, and I saw that in reader comments.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有些人没明白，我在读者的评论中看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Occasionally, I got letters about it.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，我会收到关于此事的信件。

sentences.en: You know, there were always these reminders that whatever people think of your words, it's really the stars that they want, you know?
sentences.zh: 你知道，总有人提醒我，无论人们怎么看你的文字，他们真正想要的是星级，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So, you know, that was always kind of nipping at my heels.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，那总是像是在我身后紧追不舍。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I started hearing from people higher up at the Times, or I had some discussions with my editor.
sentences.zh: 我开始收到《时报》高层的消息，或者我和我的编辑进行了一些讨论。

sentences.en: The first time it was mentioned,
sentences.zh: 第一次提到的时候，

sentences.en: I thought it was just way too soon.
